newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end up, spots down.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end up, spots down.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed up across the board in active trading on Monday due to strong domestic A share markets, traders said.
The annual rate for the most active seven-day contract rose to 9.00 percent from 8.79 percent last Friday.
Total turnover of the six-contract market soared to 6.42 million lots from 3.57 million.
One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
Traders said the bullish A share markets were the major factor supporting the repo rates on Monday.
"Some big institutions borrowed heavily from the repo market today due to the strong A share markets," one trader said.
Traders said they expected the repo rates to move slightly up on Tuesday if the A share markets continue their bull run.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mostly down on Monday mainly with the bullish A share markets absorbing funds from the spot market, traders said.
The most active three-year bond that matures in August 1999 fell to 106.78 yuan from 116.95 yuan.
Combined volume of the seven-contract market fell to 1.1 million lots from 1.4 million lots.
Traders said some short-term investors withdrew their funds from the spot market to speculate in A shares.
The spot contracts will continue to consolidate in the next few days if the A share prices rise further, traders said.
